      "explanation":"household",

      "reasoning":"A shared home address plausibly reflects ordinary household purchasing. The passed identity and issuer-authentication check supports legitimate ordering, although the recently registered home does not qualify for the household exception."

      "explanation":"synthetic_identity",

      "reasoning":"Address linkage on a recently opened account raises a possible coordinated-identity explanation. Successful identity verification, no normalized-email duplication and no device sharing weaken it."

  "disposition":"clear",
  "citations":["R08","FP-2 §6.4(b)","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(a)","FP-2 §8.1"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R08 holds because the shipping address is shared by three accounts. Although it is the account's home, its recent registration prevents the household exception. Linkage is the only adverse family; no other rule holds, and no earlier outcome settles the order. Under §6.6(b), Linkage required id_check. That check passed, satisfying every required check, so §5.3(a) requires clear and prohibits further friction. Ordinary household sharing is the strongest benign explanation; coordinated identity misuse is weakened by verification. No installments were due, so repayment intent cannot be inferred. No further check is needed."
